title: Machine-readable ARMv8.2-A compatibility baseline for armmac-generic-v1
purpose: Authoritative adjudication table for the macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) vma2 compatibility census. A finding may only be reported as incompatible if a rule in this file says so; anything not covered must be reported as NEEDS_REVIEW.

field_docs.target: The armmac-generic-v1 configuration itself: ISA level, required and excluded features, the Exception levels the payload runs at.
field_docs.verdict_vocabulary: The closed set of verdicts a rule can assign. Scanners must emit exactly these strings.
field_docs.features: One entry per Arm architectural feature plus vendor pseudo-features. Fields: name; optional_from (first architecture version at which an implementation MAY include it); mandatory_from (first version at which it MUST be included, empty if never mandatory in Armv8); in_baseline (true | false | "REQ" meaning a mainline hard requirement); verdict; note.
field_docs.sysreg_whitelist: One entry per system register encoding. Fields: name; op0; op1; crn; crm; op2; encoding (the s<op0>_<op1>_c<CRn>_c<CRm>_<op2> generic form a disassembler would print); min_el (lowest Exception level at which the encoding is architecturally accessible); feature (gating feature or null); verdict; note. Entries with verdict != IN_BASELINE are present on purpose: the table is a classification table, not only an allow-list.
field_docs.impdef_rules: Rules for deciding whether an encoding falls in IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED space, plus one negative rule recording a detection method that must NOT be used.
field_docs.undefined_ranges: Instruction-encoding ranges that are UDF, UNALLOCATED, claimed by an excluded extension, or vendor private. Each entry carries a match object with hex mask/value strings so a scanner can test (word & mask) == value, an optional exclude clause, and optional nested subranges.
field_docs.instruction_rules: Bitmask rules for instruction classes that depend on an excluded feature, most importantly the split between PAC encodings that fault and PAC encodings that are architecturally NOPs.
field_docs.host_environment: What QEMU TCG and KVM can and cannot do for this baseline.
field_docs.observed: Measurements taken from the actual 25G83 vma2 BootKC, so the baseline can be sanity-checked against reality. Includes an explicit caveat about linear scanning.
field_docs.scanner_requirements: Normative requirements a conformant scanner must satisfy.
field_docs.unverified: Claims that could NOT be established from the sources consulted. Nothing here may be used as a basis for an incompatible verdict.
field_docs.sources: URL table referenced by the sources[] field of individual rules.

verdict_vocabulary.IN_BASELINE: Guaranteed present and usable on every armmac-generic-v1 PE. No action.
verdict_vocabulary.OUT_OF_BASELINE_FATAL: Outside the baseline AND the access or execution raises an exception on a baseline PE. Must be removed, emulated, or the baseline must be widened.
verdict_vocabulary.OUT_OF_BASELINE_BENIGN: Outside the baseline but architecturally harmless on a baseline PE: executes as a NOP, or reads as zero in the ID register space. No patching required; only semantic reliance on it is a problem.
verdict_vocabulary.IMPDEF: Inside an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED encoding space. Behaviour is vendor-specific and UNDEFINED on any PE that does not define it. Always outside the baseline.
verdict_vocabulary.VENDOR_PRIVATE: A known vendor extension occupying architecturally UNALLOCATED encoding space. Always outside the baseline.
verdict_vocabulary.NEEDS_REVIEW: Not classified by this baseline. Must be adjudicated by hand; must NOT be reported as compatible.

target.note: ARMv8.0 downgrade is explicitly a future legacy-armv8 branch, not this baseline.

features.name: FEAT_FP
features.note: Floating point. Mainline hard requirement; CPACR_EL1.FPEN must be opened by the guest kernel.

features.name: FEAT_LSE
features.note: Large System Extensions (LDADD/CAS/SWP...). Mainline hard requirement; mandatory from Armv8.1 so guaranteed on any Armv8.2-A PE.

features.name: FEAT_TGran16K
features.note: 16 KiB stage-1 translation granule. OPTIONAL at every Armv8.x level - advertised by ID_AA64MMFR0_EL1.TGran16. Mainline hard requirement, therefore a host/CPU selection constraint, not a guest-side choice.

features.name: FEAT_GICv3
features.note: GICv3 CPU interface (ICC_*_EL1). Presence advertised by ID_AA64PFR0_EL1.GIC. Mainline requirement.

features.name: FEAT_AdvancedTimer
features.note: Arm Generic Timer (CNTFRQ/CNTPCT/CNTVCT/CNTV_*). Name is descriptive, not an official FEAT_ id - see unverified[].

features.name: FEAT_RAS
features.note: RAS extension (ERRIDR_EL1/DISR_EL1/ERX*). Mandatory from Armv8.2, so inside the baseline, but the guest must not depend on any error-record content.

features.name: FEAT_FP16
features.note: Half-precision FP data processing. Optional at Armv8.2; not a mainline requirement. Unconditional use is UNDEF on a PE with ID_AA64PFR0_EL1.FP != 0b0001.

features.name: FEAT_LSE2
features.note: Single-copy atomicity relaxation. No new instructions; affects only unaligned-access atomicity guarantees. Out of baseline but cannot raise an exception.

features.name: FEAT_LRCPC
features.note: LDAPR/LDAPRB/LDAPRH. Optional at Armv8.2, mandatory only from Armv8.3. UNDEF when ID_AA64ISAR1_EL1.LRCPC == 0.

features.name: FEAT_CCIDX
features.note: Extended cache-index format for CCSIDR_EL1. Changes a register layout only.

features.name: FEAT_SPE
features.note: Statistical Profiling (PMS*/PMB* at op0=3, op1=0, CRn=9).

features.name: FEAT_SVE
features.note: Scalable Vector Extension. Optional at Armv8.2, never mandatory in Armv8; mandatory only from Armv9.0. Explicitly excluded by the mainline. SVE encodings occupy the top-level group bits[28:25]==0b0010 and are UNDEF without FEAT_SVE.

features.name: FEAT_PAuth
features.note: Pointer Authentication. NOTE: introduced as OPTIONAL at Armv8.2 and mandatory only from Armv8.3 - so 'PAC is an Armv8.3 feature' is a simplification. Explicitly excluded by the mainline. See instruction_rules for the two encoding classes.

features.name: FEAT_EPAC
features.note: Enhanced PAC (AUT* poisons the pointer instead of only clearing).

features.name: FEAT_FPAC
features.note: AUT* faults directly on authentication failure.

features.name: FEAT_PACIMP
features.note: IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED PAC algorithm. Apple arm64e uses an IMP-DEF algorithm; signatures are therefore not reproducible on any other PE.

features.name: FEAT_NV
features.note: Nested virtualization. EL2-only; irrelevant to an EL1 guest payload.

features.name: FEAT_MPAM
features.note: Memory partitioning and monitoring (MPAM*_EL1 at CRn=10, CRm=5).

features.name: FEAT_VPIPT
features.note: VMID-aware PIPT i-cache; removed from later revisions of the architecture.

features.name: FEAT_LVA
features.note: 52-bit VA with 64 KiB granule. Not available with a 16 KiB granule before FEAT_LPA2.

features.name: FEAT_XNX
features.note: Stage-2 execute-never per EL. Stage 2 is the hypervisor's business, not the guest's.

features.name: FEAT_VHE
features.note: Virtualization Host Extensions. EL2 feature; an EL1 guest payload must not touch *_EL12 / *_EL2 encodings. Mandatory version not established - see unverified[].

features.name: FEAT_PMUv3
features.note: Performance Monitors v3. The mainline explicitly does NOT require PMU availability, so every PMU register access is out of baseline and must be ID-gated on ID_AA64DFR0_EL1.PMUVer.

features.name: FEAT_CSV2
features.note: Cache speculation variant 2; ID-reported only at Armv8.2.

features.name: FEAT_CSV3
features.note: Cache speculation variant 3; ID-reported only at Armv8.2.

features.name: FEAT_SPECRES
features.note: CFP/DVP/CPP RCTX prediction-restriction instructions (op0=0b01 SYS space).

features.name: FEAT_SB
features.note: SB speculation barrier. Introduced version not established - see unverified[].

features.name: FEAT_IDST
features.note: ID-space accesses trap to EL2 rather than being UNDEF.

features.name: FEAT_BTI
features.note: Branch Target Identification. Explicitly excluded by the mainline. BTI is encoded in the HINT space (HINT #32..#38), so on a PE without FEAT_BTI a BTI instruction executes as a NOP and the guarded-page attribute is simply not enforced - benign, not fatal.

features.name: FEAT_MTE
features.note: Instruction-only Memory Tagging. Explicitly excluded. Commonly described as an Armv8.5 feature - the 8.4-vs-8.5 introduction level is listed as unverified[].

features.name: FEAT_MTE2
features.note: Full MTE (tag checking, TFSR_EL1, GCR_EL1, IRG/ADDG/SUBG/STG/LDG...).

features.name: FEAT_AMUv1
features.note: Activity Monitors (AMCR_EL0 etc. at CRn=13). Introduced version listed as unverified[].

features.name: FEAT_SME
features.note: Scalable Matrix Extension. Explicitly excluded. Control register SVCR is op0=3, op1=3, CRn=4, CRm=2, op2=2; SME instruction encodings occupy the top-level group bit[31]==1 && bits[28:25]==0b0000. Observed 5 SVCR accesses in the 25G83 vma2 BootKC.

features.name: APPLE_AMX
features.note: Apple Matrix coprocessor. No Arm FEAT_ id. Occupies 0x00201000-0x002012DF inside the A64 top-level Reserved/UNALLOCATED group. 163 AMX words observed in the 25G83 vma2 BootKC (AMX_LDX/LDY/STX/STY/LDZ/STZ/SET/CLR).

features.name: APPLE_GXF
features.note: Apple Guarded Exception Levels (GL1/GL2). genter = 0x00201420 | imm5, gexit = 0x00201400. Zero occurrences in the 25G83 vma2 BootKC - macOS uses PPL rather than SPTM, so GXF is not a blocker for this target.

features.name: APPLE_SPRR
features.note: Apple Sealed/Shadow Permission Remap Registers, e.g. SPRR_CONFIG_EL1 = s3_6_c15_c1_0. IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED system register space.

features.name: APPLE_WKDM
features.note: Apple hardware page compressor/decompressor. wkdmc = 0x00200800 | rD<<5 | rS, wkdmd = 0x00200C00 | rD<<5 | rS.

features.name: APPLE_AT_AS1ELX
features.note: Apple address-translation instruction at 0x00201440 | rA; result returned in the same register in a PAR_EL1-like format.

decode.note: bits[31:22]==0b1101010100 selects the System instruction class; bit21=L (0=MSR,1=MRS); bits[20:19]=op0; bits[18:16]=op1; bits[15:12]=CRn; bits[11:8]=CRm; bits[7:5]=op2; bits[4:0]=Rt. op0>=2 is the MRS/MSR register form.

impdef_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: UNDEFINED unless the specific PE defines the register. A standard Armv8.2-A PE (and QEMU/KVM) does not, so the access raises an Undefined Instruction exception.
impdef_rules.rationale: Arm reserves the whole op0=0b11, CRn=0b1011 and op0=0b11, CRn=0b1111 encoding space for IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED registers. Both halves are genuinely used by Arm's own cores: Cortex-A57 places CPUACTLR_EL1 at S3_1_C15_C2_0 and L2CTLR_EL1 at S3_1_C11_C0_2.
impdef_rules.confidence: high (rule corroborated by three independent implementations); DDI 0487 section number NOT quoted - see unverified[]

decode.note: Same class encoding with bits[20:19]==0b01 (op0=0b01). This is the DC/IC/AT/TLBI/prediction-restriction space.

impdef_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: UNDEFINED on a PE that does not define the operation.
impdef_rules.rationale: Arm's own cores place IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED system operations in this space, e.g. the Cortex-A57 RAMINDEX operation at CRn=c15.
impdef_rules.confidence: medium - inferred from vendor TRMs, not quoted from DDI 0487

impdef_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: The encoding is architectural, so the access does NOT fault; only the value is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED. QEMU implements these as constants (0) or RAZ/WI.
impdef_rules.rationale: Distinguish 'IMP-DEF encoding space' (faults) from 'architectural encoding with IMP-DEF content' (does not fault). Code that reads these is portable; code that branches on their value is not.

impdef_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: Reads as zero. Unallocated slots inside the ID register space must RAZ rather than be UNDEF, so that a future architecture version can define a register there. A read therefore never faults, whatever the architecture level of the PE.
impdef_rules.rationale: An encoding such as s3_0_c0_c4_2 (ID_AA64PFR2_EL1, Armv8.9) has no meaning on an Armv8.2-A PE, but it is NOT in IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED space and it does NOT fault. Classifying every unnamed encoding as IMP-DEF produces false positives here. Reading such a slot is benign; branching on a non-zero result is what would be wrong.
impdef_rules.confidence: high - stated explicitly in QEMU's v8 ID register definitions and consistent with the Linux ID-register emulation ABI

impdef_rules.rationale: A disassembler renders an unknown system register as s<op0>_<op1>_c<CRn>_c<CRm>_<op2>. Testing for the substring '_c15_' therefore ALSO matches CRm==15 at an arbitrary CRn (for example s3_0_c2_c15_0, which is not IMP-DEF), and misses the whole CRn==11 IMP-DEF half. Classification must be done on the decoded CRn field, never on the rendered string.

undefined_ranges.behaviour_on_baseline: Permanently UNDEFINED. Raises an Undefined Instruction exception at the current EL (ESR_ELx.EC = 0b000000, 'Unknown reason').
undefined_ranges.decode_path: top level: bit[31]==0 && bits[28:25]==0b0000 -> Reserved group; inside it bits[30:29]==0b00 && bits[24:16]==0b000000000 -> UDF

undefined_ranges.behaviour_on_baseline: UNALLOCATED. Behaves as UNDEFINED on a conformant PE; a future architecture version may allocate it.
undefined_ranges.decode_path: top level: bit[31]==0 && bits[28:25]==0b0000 -> Reserved group; inside it, anything other than (bits[30:29]==0b00 && bits[24:16]==0) is UNALLOCATED
undefined_ranges.note: This is the group that contains every Apple private instruction observed so far.

undefined_ranges.claimed_by: FEAT_SVE (optional from Armv8.2, mandatory from Armv9.0)
undefined_ranges.behaviour_on_baseline: UNDEFINED, because armmac-generic-v1 excludes FEAT_SVE. Not UNALLOCATED: the space is allocated to SVE, so it must not be reused for anything else.

undefined_ranges.note: SME sits in the bit31==1 half of the same top-level group that holds Reserved/UNALLOCATED in the bit31==0 half. Apple's private space is in the bit31==0 half, so SME and Apple AMX do NOT collide.

undefined_ranges.behaviour_on_baseline: Every word in this range is UNALLOCATED under the Arm architecture (checked against the 2026-03 release of the A64 machine-readable spec) and is therefore UNDEFINED on a standard Armv8.2-A PE and under QEMU TCG / KVM. No Arm extension, including SVE and SME, claims any part of it.
undefined_ranges.decode_path: bit[31]==0, bits[30:29]==0b00, bits[28:25]==0b0000, bits[24:21]==0b0001 -> inside the Reserved group with op1!=0 -> UNALLOCATED
undefined_ranges.apple_note: Apple's ESR on its own silicon reports an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED EC (0b111111) when AMX is disabled; a standard PE reports EC=0b000000 instead. Do not pattern-match on Apple's ESR values.

legacy_scanner_mask.comment: The mask used by scan_incompatible.py covers 0x00200000-0x003FFFFF, i.e. wider than Apple's documented 0x0020xxxx usage but still a strict subset of A64_RESERVED_UNALLOCATED.

match.extra: bits[15:10] <= 0b010001; additionally, for bits[15:10] >= 0b001000 (the Z and XPAC forms) Rn (bits[9:5]) must be 0b11111, otherwise the word is itself an unallocated encoding in the same group

instruction_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: UNDEFINED. Arm's decode pseudocode for the Integer class reads: if FEAT_PAuth is not implemented then EndOfDecode(Decode_UNDEF).

match.note: bits[20:16] are the fixed field 0b11111, Rn is bits[9:5] and Rm is bits[4:0]; bit10 selects key A vs B

instruction_rules.note: Encoding: bits[31:24]=0b11111000, bit23=0, bit22=key(A/B), bit21=1, bits[20:12]=imm9, bit11=W, bit10=1. Capstone 5.x decodes these but renders both keys as 'ldraa', so the key must be read from bit22 rather than from the mnemonic.

instruction_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: Executes as a NOP. Arm's decode pseudocode for the System class of these instructions reads: if FEAT_PAuth is not implemented then EndOfDecode(Decode_NOP). No exception, no patching required.
instruction_rules.critical: This is the single most important split in the whole baseline. The HINT-space forms are free; the Integer and Branch classes are hard faults. A scanner that ignores 'pac*'/'aut*' by mnemonic collapses the two and reports zero problems.

instruction_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: Unallocated encodings in the HINT space execute as a NOP. This is the structural reason both the PAC HINT forms and BTI are benign rather than fatal: the architecture puts them where an unaware PE simply ignores them.
instruction_rules.note: The exact DDI 0487 wording was not quoted - see unverified[]. Verified behaviourally against Capstone 5.x, which renders unallocated values in this space as 'hint #N' (e.g. 0xD503243F -> hint #0x21).
instruction_rules.scanner_guidance: Do NOT report anything in this space as fatal. Report it only if the guest relies on the hint's semantics.

instruction_rules.behaviour_on_baseline: Executes as a NOP on a PE without FEAT_BTI; the guarded-page attribute is simply not enforced. No patching required.

findings: There is no '-cpu armv8.2-a' generic model. QEMU exposes named models plus 'max'.
Two shipped TCG models are genuine Armv8.2-A implementations and are much closer to armmac-generic-v1 than 'max' is: cortex-a76 and neoverse-n1.

neoverse-n1 ID registers in QEMU master: ID_AA64ISAR0=0x0000100010211120 (Atomic=2 -> FEAT_LSE, CRC32=1, RDM=1), ID_AA64ISAR1=0x0000000000100001 (DPB=1, LRCPC=1, APA=0, API=0, GPA=0, GPI=0 -> no PAC at all), ID_AA64PFR0=0x1100000010111112 (SVE field = 0), ID_AA64PFR1=0x0000000000000020 (BT=0 -> no BTI, MTE=0 -> no MTE), ID_AA64MMFR0=0x0000000000101125 (TGran16=1 -> 16 KiB granule supported, PARange=5 -> 48-bit PA).
cortex-a76 is identical except ID_AA64MMFR0=0x0000000000101122 (PARange=2 -> 40-bit PA) and ID_AA64PFR1=0x10.
So: '-cpu neoverse-n1' already gives ARMv8.2-A + FEAT_LSE + 16 KiB granule + FP/AdvSIMD with PAC, BTI, MTE, SVE and SME all absent. It does set ARM_FEATURE_PMU.

On '-cpu max' the relevant knobs are: pauth=off (disables FEAT_PAuth entirely), sve=off, sme=off, pmu=off. There is no documented bti=off or mte=off CPU property; MTE on the virt machine is gated by the machine option rather than a CPU property.
Recommendation for the project: use -cpu neoverse-n1 (or cortex-a76) for baseline conformance testing rather than -cpu max with knobs, because the named models are a fixed, reviewable feature set.
ID_AA64* are trapped and emulated by KVM. The guest can only read them; it cannot write them, so the guest kernel cannot fake feature presence or absence.

Userspace (QEMU) may write ID registers via KVM_SET_ONE_REG, but only before the VM has run and only to a value that is a subset of KVM's sanitised limit, which is derived from the host CPU. arm64_check_features() rejects any attempt to advertise more than the limit with -E2BIG, reported to userspace as -EINVAL. After the VM has run the registers are immutable (-EBUSY).

Consequence 1: features can be HIDDEN from the guest but never ADDED. PAC present on the host can be masked off so XNU's ID-gated arm64e probes see APA=API=0 - but that does nothing about already-compiled PAC instructions in the kernelcache, which still fault.

Consequence 2: FEAT_TGran16 is a host CPU selection constraint. If the host does not implement a 16 KiB stage-1 granule the guest cannot have one, and the 16 KiB mainline requirement fails before any loader work matters. For reference, QEMU's cortex-a72 model reports ID_AA64MMFR0=0x00001124 with TGran16=0, while cortex-a55/a76/neoverse-n1 all report TGran16=1.
Consequence 3: per-field writability of ID registers varies by kernel version and was not measured on the target host - see unverified[].

observed.method: linear 4-byte scan of the single executable segment, bitmask classification, random sample cross-checked against Capstone 5.x
observed.caveat: This is a LINEAR scan, not a code-coverage proof. Literal pools inside __TEXT_EXEC inflate the UDF and Reserved buckets (41737 words land in the UDF pattern and roughly 250 of the 418 Reserved hits are plainly data such as 0x01000100). Counts for the PAC and system-register classes are reliable because their encodings do not look like small constants; counts for the Reserved/UDF group are upper bounds only.
observed.pac_fatal_vs_benign: 497541 instructions fault on a PE without FEAT_PAuth; 125616 are architecturally NOPs. Both sets are invisible to macos-arm64-compat-scanner/scan_incompatible.py.
observed.self_check: Every mask rule in instruction_rules was applied back to this image. Results: PAC_INTEGER_CLASS 234238, PAC_PACGA 17, PAC_BRANCH_CLASS_Z 80662, PAC_BRANCH_CLASS_REG 182624, PAC_AUTHENTICATED_LOAD 0, PAC_HINT_CLASS 125616, BTI_HINT 64827. Fatal total 497541 and benign total 190443 match analysis/compat/summary.json (PAC/block 497541, PAC/degrade 125616, BTI/degrade 64827), which was produced by separate tooling.
observed.impdef_note: All 13 distinct IMP-DEF encodings use CRn=15 with op1 in {3,4,5,6}. CRn=11 is unused by this binary. The baseline still has to cover CRn=11, because the rule is architectural and other Apple images or future BootKCs may use it.

scanner_requirements: Classify system registers on the DECODED (op0, op1, CRn, CRm, op2) tuple, never on a disassembler-rendered name.
Treat op0=0b11 with CRn in {0b1011, 0b1111} as IMPDEF; do not special-case CRn=15 alone.
Treat op0=0b01 with CRn in {0b1011, 0b1111} as suspected IMPDEF system instructions.
Resolve every architectural encoding against sysreg_whitelist and report anything absent as NEEDS_REVIEW, not as compatible. The whitelist is not complete - see unverified[].
Report EL2/EL3-only encodings reached from EL1 code as OUT_OF_BASELINE_FATAL.
Detect PAC by bitmask, splitting the Integer/Branch/Load classes (fatal) from the HINT class (benign). Never filter PAC out by mnemonic.
Detect the Reserved/UNALLOCATED groups by the top-level decode rules, not by a hand-written list of a few vendor opcodes.
Separate code from data before reporting counts. Literal pools inside __TEXT_EXEC produce large numbers of words that match the UDF and Reserved patterns.
Scan every 4-byte word of every executable range, including the last instruction of each function.
Load this JSON rather than embedding a whitelist in source.
unverified: DDI 0487 could not be quoted directly: every developer.arm.com fetch in this session returned HTTP 403. The IMP-DEF system register rule (op0=0b11, CRn in {0b1011,0b1111}) is therefore stated without a section number, backed instead by Arm Trusted Firmware (Cortex-A57 CPUACTLR_EL1 = S3_1_C15_C2_0, L2CTLR_EL1 = S3_1_C11_C0_2), QEMU's IMPDEF register definitions, and the Linux arm64 documentation statement that no IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED register is exposed.
Whether op0=0b01 (SYS/SYSL) CRn in {11,15} is the complete IMP-DEF system-instruction rule: not verified. Inferred from vendor TRM usage only.
The IMP-DEF subspace rule for op0=0b10 (debug/trace): not verified at all. Scanners should report op0=2 encodings outside sysreg_whitelist as NEEDS_REVIEW.

FEAT_MTE introduction level: the feature table used here says optional from Armv8.4, while Arm's public material usually presents MTE as an Armv8.5 feature. Not resolved. The baseline verdict is unaffected because MTE is excluded either way.

Mandatory versions for FEAT_VHE, FEAT_RDM, FEAT_VMID16, FEAT_XNX, FEAT_PMUv3p1, FEAT_SPE, FEAT_LVA, FEAT_LPA and FEAT_IESB are blank in the table used, and were not confirmed from Arm directly. This baseline makes no claim about their mandatory status. In particular, FEAT_VHE is widely described as mandatory from Armv8.1, which this document does NOT assert.

'FEAT_AdvancedTimer' and 'FEAT_GICv3' are project-local labels, not Arm FEAT_ identifiers. The Generic Timer is part of the Armv8-A architecture rather than a named optional feature, and GICv3 is defined by the GIC architecture specification (IHI 0069) with PE-side availability reported in ID_AA64PFR0_EL1.GIC.
FEAT_AMUv1 introduction version (listed here as Armv8.4): not verified item by item.

The Apple private sub-ranges come from Asahi Linux reverse-engineering notes, not from Arm or Apple. Note that asahilinux.org's SPRR/GXF page lists BOTH genter and gexit as 0x00201420, which is self-contradictory; this baseline uses the Asahi 'HW:Apple Instructions' page values (gexit = 0x00201400, genter = 0x00201420 | imm5). Neither was independently verified.
The exact extent of APPLE_MUL53 (0x00200000-0x002007FF) and the semantics of the 0x002012E0-0x0020143F hole are reverse-engineered third-party claims.
Per-field ID-register writability under KVM varies by kernel version and was not measured on any target host.

sysreg_whitelist completeness: this table covers the main EL1/EL0-reachable architectural registers but was NOT reconciled entry by entry against Arm Architecture Registers (DDI 0601). Missing entries must be adjudicated as NEEDS_REVIEW.
ETE/ETM trace register block (op0=2, op1=1) is represented by a single placeholder entry and not enumerated.
RVBAR_EL1 accessibility from EL1 inside a KVM guest (where EL2 exists) was not verified.
Whether QEMU exposes a bti=off or mte=off CPU property on any model: not found in the documentation consulted; treated as 'not available'.

The rule 'unallocated encodings in the HINT space execute as a NOP' is stated without a DDI 0487 quote. It is consistent with the PACIA System-class decode pseudocode (Decode_NOP) and with how disassemblers render the space, but the normative sentence was not retrieved.

The GXF instruction pair is named genter/gexit in every source found. No source describes instructions named 'gcall' or 'gret', so the task's reference to gcall/gret is treated as a naming mismatch rather than a separate instruction pair that still needs locating.
